title: Kahan-stable Heron formula and exact area equivalence

problemStatement.formal: kahan_product(a,b,c) = 16 * heron_product(a,b,c), and for valid triangle sides kahan_area(a,b,c) = triangle_area(a,b,c).
problemStatement.plain: This entry records the exact Lean proof that Kahan's rearranged Heron formula agrees with the classical area formula while keeping each algebraic factor well behaved for nearly degenerate triangles.
whyMatters: Connects a classical geometry formula to a numerically stable computation pattern.
Shows the equality and non-negativity facts can be proved by elementary real algebra rather than left as informal numerical-analysis commentary.

proven: `kahan_product` and `heron_product` define the stable and classical products.
`kahan_product_nonneg` and `heron_product_nonneg` prove non-negativity under triangle inequalities.
`kahan_area_eq_triangle_area` proves the stable area formula equals the classical Heron area.
`kahan_factors_nonneg_ordered`, `kahan_product_345`, `kahan_area_345`, and `kahan_area_5_12_13` document the ordered-factor and numerical-example behavior.
open: Floating-point rounding-error bounds are discussed mathematically but not formalized.
Related Heron/Brahmagupta entries handle adjacent inequalities and should stay separate from this exact Kahan identity file.
knownResults.goal: Use the axiom-free Kahan identity as the stable-area bridge before adding any true floating-point error model.
